“They say still unto them that despise me, The Lord hath said, Ye shall have peace”. They are speaking to people who really hate God. At the sit down, the man with the hat kept saying that when tribulation comes, we're not going to be here; the church won't be here. Christians just lie and tell you there's going to be peace.

But Paul and Barnabas were “Confirming the souls of the disciples, and exhorting them to continue in the faith, and that we must through much tribulation enter into the kingdom of God.” The only way we're entering the kingdom of God is through much tribulation. So what Bible are these Christians reading?

That is why Jeremiah says “Hearken not unto the words of the prophets that prophesy unto you: they make you vain: they speak a vision of their own heart, and not out of the mouth of the Lord.” A vision of their own heart is their own mind, what they feel at that moment: I don't know who this is for, but God has a message for you. It is not coming from the Bible, and the Bible says tribulation.

precepts.why:
Paul and Barnabas went about “Confirming the souls of the disciples, and exhorting them to continue in the faith, and that we must through much tribulation enter into the kingdom of God.” The tribulation hasn't fully started; you see it on a certain scale, but it will intensify. It will get worse, and worse, and worse.

Micah says how to go through it: “Be in pain, and labour to bring forth, O daughter of Zion, like a woman in travail”. The Bible says to be in pain. Pain is coming, and it has already begun; pay attention to what Trump and these people are doing. But whatever pain you go through, you still have to labour, labouring in this truth.

“for now shalt thou go forth out of the city, and thou shalt dwell in the field, and thou shalt go even to Babylon”. Where are we living today? Babylon: Mystery Babylon the Great, the United States of America.

Why does it say like a woman in travail? Because the pain comes and it goes, and when the baby is close to coming the pains increase and get worse and worse. That is what you see taking place now. Whether this society has another ten or twenty years, as the time draws nearer the pains will increase: the affliction rising against those of us that fear God. Keep labouring through them.

That is why the brother who is not studying and applying the scriptures has no root and will not survive it; when things get real he will be offended, scared, and go back into the world. Sisters, a brother who never teaches and is never in a camp video is a gamble.

note.label: Cyber Warfare: The Mouth Of The Beast

precepts.why:
Much tribulation is coming, and Revelation shows where it comes from: “And the dragon was wroth with the woman”. The dragon is the beast, the white man, Esau. According to the prophecy they will be angry at us, “and went to make war with the remnant of her seed”.

Why? Not because we are evil or terrorists, but because we “keep the commandments of God, and have the testimony of Jesus Christ.” The testimony of Jesus Christ is everything written in this book, everything the prophets said would happen, everything written about who the wicked are and all the evil the so-called white man is doing. That testimony says these people are the synagogue of Satan, and that God is bringing judgment on them for all their evil on the earth. As you teach it, they get angry and make war with us.

So do not think we will be out there teaching the Bible and everything will be good. The tribulation will be attacks from the government: labelling us a hate group, lying on us, putting us in prison, hitting your pocket and your food, attacking your wife and your children, because those are the things we care about. In the end they will force idol worship: worship the beast, or you can't buy, sell, work, get a job or go to the doctor.

The dragon is wroth, and he will make war with us. That is the much tribulation through which we must enter into the kingdom of God, and why we must be exhorted to continue in the faith.

precepts.text: We must through much tribulation enter into the kingdom of God, as our forefather Joseph did.
precepts.point: Jacob knew there was corn in Egypt because Joseph had already told Pharaoh exactly what to do to save up in the time of tribulation; when Jacob heard, he sent out the fathers. Applying these attributes makes better men, women, brothers, and sisters, to bring forth the nation unto the kingdom of God.

note.label: Genesis 45: Joseph Made Known unto His Brethren

precepts.why:
“Confirming the souls of the disciples, and exhorting them to continue in the faith, and that we must through much tribulation enter into the kingdom of God.” There is no other way into the kingdom but through tribulation. Our forefather Joseph went through it: the pit, the slavery, the prison, and then the governorship of Egypt.

When trials come, read the afflictions of the forefathers and the attributes they had in those times, and apply them: forgiveness, favor, righteousness, mercy. That is continuing in the faith through much tribulation.

note.label: Psalm 55: Cast Thy Burden Upon the Lord

precepts.why:

But the scriptures say we must serve out this punishment: Paul and Barnabas were “Confirming the souls of the disciples, and exhorting them to continue in the faith, and that we must through much tribulation enter into the kingdom of God.”

We must through much tribulation enter into the kingdom. The four chapters a day is part of that exhortation to continue in the faith. Our eyes have been enlightened to why these things happen. George Floyd and Breonna Taylor got the most news for 2020, but many of our people have suffered getting beat and murdered, like the brother they found in the cornfield. There is no flying away from it; we endure it into the kingdom.

note.label: Psalm 73: God Is Good to Israel

precepts.why:
The psalmist says, “Thus my heart was grieved, and I was pricked in my reins. So foolish was I, and ignorant: I was as a beast before thee.” He was grieved watching the wicked prosper. “Nevertheless I am continually with thee: thou hast holden me by my right hand.” He snapped back to his senses and realized the wicked are set for destruction.

Paul and Barnabas taught the same, “Confirming the souls of the disciples, and exhorting them to continue in the faith, and that we must through much tribulation enter into the kingdom of God.” Those afflicted are being prepared. We must go through much afflictions to enter the kingdom, whether financial, spiritual, physical or mental.

So the grief and the affliction are not a sign that the Most High has left. He holds us by the right hand through it, and “Thou shalt guide me with thy counsel, and afterward receive me to glory.” The tribulation is the road into the kingdom.

Who were those Gentiles? The northern kingdom, that was also scattered abroad; so it was open to them. Once Christ opens that door there is no man that can shut it. Remember, the scribes and Pharisees tried to shut it: no, no, they can't come in, they're this and they're that, you have to sacrifice. They tried to shut it, but there is no power on earth that can shut it. You have men and women online right now saying the northern kingdom is not Israel. God don't give a damn what you say or think or how many videos you put out; you are not stopping nothing. You can sit on Facebook, YouTube, Periscope, whatever platform: you cannot shut the door the Lord opens.

In Iconium, Paul and Barnabas so spake that a great multitude both of the Jews and also of the Greeks believed. Paul was not stationary; he was not local; he was traveling, moving around and around.

Long time therefore abode they speaking boldly in the Lord. They were not bashful. When an assault was made to stone them, they were ware of it, and fled unto Lystra and Derbe, cities of Lycaonia. And there they preached the gospel. How did they preach it? Boldly.

The people of Lystra saw what Paul had done and called Barnabas, Jupiter; and Paul, Mercurius, because he was the chief speaker, and the priest of Jupiter brought oxen and garlands to do sacrifice unto them. The apostles rent their clothes and ran in among the people, crying out, We also are men of like passions with you, and preach unto you that ye should turn from these vanities unto the living God. Stop this nonsense; turn to the living God and keep the commandments.

Then certain Jews from Antioch and Iconium persuaded the people, and having stoned Paul, drew him out of the city, supposing he had been dead. They knocked Paul upside the head with stones, and he went to the third heavens: that is the vision he spoke of in 2 Corinthians 12.

Howbeit, as the disciples stood round about him, he rose up, and came into the city: and the next day he departed with Barnabas to Derbe. And when they had preached the gospel to that city, and had taught many, they returned again to Lystra, and to Iconium, and Antioch. They went right back. Just like the team in Kenya: when they stoned us, we went right back. We took those stones, brothers got hit in the jaw, and we came right back. We are not going anywhere.
